analysis:
The supplied units contain only CHANGELOG.md text: the base excerpts cover lines 1311-1801 and the head excerpt covers lines 1-221. No code, authorization logic, crypto or config changed here, so no concrete regression can be shown from this file alone. The new head entries claim code changes that were not supplied, so those claims are unverified. Items for the code-bearing passes to check:
- SSD prefix cache (T-041, A-001; head lines 14, 28-32): the cache storage controls pin volume UUID, require encryption for external volumes and keep keys and the write ledger on the Mac. The demanded checkpoint writes give repeated authenticated checkpoints reserved SSD write share. Check that salt scoping, HMAC names, 30-minute TTL and the per-donation gate are unchanged.
- Autopilot floor (T-060, A-009; head lines 40-50): the changelog says rewards are authorized at the declaration's original receive time and floor accrual ends after 2026-11-07 UTC. It also says payments are default off, with admin pool-cap funding and baseline-repair endpoints. Check admin authorization, replay and duplicate settlement, and the origin of the baseline evidence.
- Account erasure and soft-delete (T-059, A-009; head lines 129, 135-153, 179-182): the soft-delete mutation gate defaults to false. Check erasure fences and that Stripe IDs are not left behind.
- Coordinator logs (T-051, T-058; head line 161): emails, IPs, serials and UDIDs are removed from logs. Verify this against the code.
- CI review and merge clearance (head lines 16-18, 73-81): this is outside the runtime threat model and affects only review-pipeline trust.
The changelog entries are consistent with the threat model, which is why no finding is raised. Because the code behind these claims is unavailable, this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
